recovery.title: Diagnostics and recovery
recovery.description:
**Current entry status** *(checked locally, no cloud requests)*:

{cache_icon} **Local device cache:** `{cache_reason}`
{setup_icon} **Last setup status:** `{setup_reason}`
{auth_icon} **Auth session:** `{auth_reason}`
{cloud_icon} **Cloud connectivity:** `{cloud_reason}`
{scenario_icon} **Speaker scenarios:** `{scenario_reason}`
{ownership_icon} **Speaker ownership:** `{ownership_reason}`

*🟢 — normal · 🟡 — offline/limited mode · 🔴 — needs attention*

Select an action below:

menu_options.claim_speaker: Claim speaker from a disabled account

retry_setup.title: Restart integration entry
retry_setup.description:
Performs one ordinary reload of this entry without resetting your settings or local cache.

Useful when the entry is stuck in an error state after a temporary network or Yandex outage. Manually disabled entries are not enabled automatically.

retry_scenario_creation.title: Restore speaker cloud scenario
retry_scenario_creation.description:
Use this when local control works, but cloud voice commands or cloud TTS fail on a speaker.

1. First, the integration checks the cloud scenario list — if the service scenario already exists, it will be bound without creating a new one.
2. If not found, at most one creation attempt will be performed after your confirmation.

data.confirm_risk: I understand the duplicate risk on cloud timeout and confirm the retry

claim_speaker.title: Claim speaker from another account
claim_speaker.description:
Use this when moving a speaker between Yandex accounts on the same Home Assistant instance.

• The previous owner account must be disabled or removed first.
• All speaker entities keep their entity IDs, custom names, area, and history.
• Foreign tokens and scenarios are never copied — this account uses its own cache.

data.confirm_claim: Confirm transferring speaker ownership to this account

settings.title: Integration settings and modes
settings.description: Manage offline modes and resilience policy. A custom API base URL changes the trusted endpoint for its role, but never forwards OAuth, Passport track IDs, or expanded cookie scopes to an untrusted origin. YAML ssl: false still disables TLS certificate verification, including for diagnostic MiTM proxies; cookies, tokens, and commands are then exposed to the proxy.

data.enable_diagnostic_sensors: Enable connectivity and status diagnostic sensors

data_description.quasar_base_url: HTTPS URL for Quasar API; path prefix is preserved. No userinfo, query, or fragment. Current URL: {current_quasar}. Leave empty to clear override.
data_description.account_base_url: HTTPS URL for account endpoints; path prefix is preserved. No userinfo, query, or fragment. Current URL: {current_account}. Leave empty to clear override.
data_description.passport_base_url: HTTPS URL for Passport; path prefix is preserved. Credentials are never sent to a foreign origin. Current URL: {current_passport}. Leave empty to clear override.
data_description.mobileproxy_base_url: HTTPS URL for MobileProxy; current URL: {current_mobileproxy}. Leave empty to clear override.
data_description.glagol_base_url: HTTPS URL for Glagol token API; current URL: {current_glagol}. Leave empty to clear override.
data_description.rpc_base_url: HTTPS URL for RPC; current URL: {current_rpc}. Leave empty to clear override.
data_description.cookie_storage_endpoints: Non-empty JSON array of url/validator objects (status_ok or uid_in_storage); current value: {current_cookie}. Leave empty to clear override.
data_description.csrf_endpoints: Non-empty JSON array of HTTPS URLs; current value: {current_csrf}. Leave empty to clear override.
